domain: Cancer Research and Genetic Association Database
scenario:
An international cancer research consortium is developing a comprehensive genetic database to catalog associations between genes and various types of cancer. The goal of the database is to support cancer researchers by providing detailed information about the genetic roles in cancer pathology, such as oncogenes and tumor suppressors. This system will integrate data from multiple research publications and studies, enhancing the ability to track gene-disease associations.

The platform will allow researchers to explore relationships between genetic markers and cancer types, normalized across international classification systems. It will also include citation metrics to gauge the research impact of each gene-cancer association. Researchers will be able to search and filter data by gene, cancer type, and role (e.g., Oncogene, Tumor Suppressor). 

The system must support complex queries to facilitate advanced research insights, such as identifying frequently cited genes in literature associated with specific cancer types. Additionally, the platform will provide tools for submitting new findings and updating existing records, ensuring the database remains current with ongoing research developments.

The system also needs to incorporate robust user management to control access to sensitive genetic data, with roles and permissions for researchers, curators, and administrators. The platform should facilitate collaboration among global research teams and offer reporting tools to analyze gene-disease interactions and trends.
